claim: For a>1, b>a and 0<theta<1, the one-sided interpolant G(x)<=chord(G endpoints)+D where D=chord(xlogx)-xlogx<= (b-a)^2/(8a). Choosing b-a<=sqrt(8*a^(1+theta)) makes D<=a^theta<=x^theta; G at adaptive grid nodes<=C node^theta implies G(x)<=(C+1)x^theta, with C independent of the window scale.
asymptotics: Adaptive step length ~a^((1+theta)/2), so grid count O(Y^((3/2)*(1-theta)/2)) = O(Y^(3*(1-theta)/4)) on [Y,Y^1.5]. This is conditional sampling complexity, not a method to prove bounds at each node.
proof: Positive Lambda(n)/n implies S(x)=sum Lambda(n)/n*(x-n)_+ is convex. Since G=S-xlogx+(1+gamma)x, Jensen S(x)<=chord(S) (FALSE: convex S(x) <= its chord: YES). D>=0 from convexity xlogx; D <= (b-a)^2/(8a) from upper second derivative 1/a. Concavity of x^theta gives chord(x^theta)<=x^theta. The adaptive step ensures D <= x^theta. A dyadic grouping over [Y,Y^1.5] yields O(Y^(3*(1-theta)/4)) cells; no PNT is required.
warning: No proof of RH. Error checks are float-only and do not certify an infinite set; formal inequalities are unconditional basic convexity.
